authority: End-user identity through on-behalf-of; Fabric permissions decide what is visible.
fabric_role: Owns governed context, data permissions and the data agent's curated sources.
foundry_role: Owns reasoning, orchestration, conversation and evaluation.
mcp_role: Optional transport (data agent MCP endpoint); grants no authority.
name: Fabric Data Agent + Foundry
offline_equivalent: Local deterministic data agent over the semantic model with allow-listed queries.
preview_dependencies: Foundry Agent Service Microsoft Fabric tool
summary: A Foundry agent asks a governed Fabric data agent for answers over structured Fabric data.
when_not_to_use: When a fixed report answers the question, or when service-principal-only access is required.
when_to_use: Conversational questions over curated lakehouse, warehouse or semantic-model data.

authority: Per-domain Fabric permissions under the end user's identity.
fabric_role: Domain data agents and the shared semantic layer.
name: Multiple Fabric Data Agents via Fabric IQ
offline_equivalent: Local domain routing over separate semantic subsets.
summary: A coordinating agent routes to bounded, domain-specific data agents through Fabric IQ.
when_not_to_use: One domain, or when a single bounded data agent is enough.
when_to_use: Several governed business domains with different owners and permissions.

authority: Bindings inherit the underlying item permissions.
foundry_role: Uses the ontology to ground reasoning.
mcp_role: Ontology MCP exposes entities for discovery (preview).
name: Fabric IQ Ontology
summary: Business entities, relationships and vocabulary bound to Fabric data without copying it.
when_not_to_use: A single report or app where a semantic model already carries the meaning.
when_to_use: Many consumers need one shared business vocabulary and entity model.

authority: The search service's managed identity indexes content; plan entitlement trimming explicitly.
foundry_role: Indexes, retrieves and cites; evaluates groundedness.
name: OneLake as Foundry knowledge
offline_equivalent: Local retrieval over synthetic documents with citations.
summary: Unstructured files in OneLake become cited knowledge for agents through Foundry IQ.
when_not_to_use: Numeric questions that belong to governed measures.
when_to_use: Retrieval over documents with citations, alongside structured analytics.

authority: Workspace identity and tenant settings for AI features.
fabric_role: Runs the pipeline and stores enriched results.
name: Foundry tools in Fabric (AI in data engineering)
summary: AI functions classify, extract and summarize inside notebooks and pipelines.
when_not_to_use: Interactive questions that need conversation and tools.
when_to_use: Batch enrichment that should be repeatable, reviewed and stored in Silver or Gold.

authority: Entra identity plus policy; humans approve high-impact actions.
mcp_role: Standardized tool access with allow-lists; never authorization.
name: Fabric + Foundry enterprise agent (anchor)
offline_equivalent: Local providers, deterministic agent, local evaluation and audit.
summary: An application agent combines Foundry knowledge and Fabric context with identity, evaluation, audit and approval.
when_not_to_use: Simple Q&A that one data agent or report already answers.
when_to_use: Production assistants that read governed data and may propose actions.

authority: Policy and human approval before any action.
name: Real-time Fabric + Foundry agent
summary: Operational events feed context to an agent that proposes, never autonomously executes, actions.
when_not_to_use: When a deterministic alert rule is sufficient.
when_to_use: Time-sensitive operational signals that need triage and proposed actions.

authority: Human approver plus a narrowly scoped writer identity.
fabric_role: Target of approved changes; source of context.
foundry_role: Proposes; never performs authoritative writes directly.
mcp_role: May expose a plan tool; approval stays outside MCP.
name: Human-in-the-loop governed action
offline_equivalent: Full plan, approve, simulated execute, verify and audit flow.
summary: Retrieve, cite, reason, propose, validate, apply policy, approve, scoped write, verify, audit.
when_not_to_use: Never skip it for high-impact, destructive, regulated or financially material actions.
when_to_use: Any write to a business system or Fabric item.

authority: Entra identity and the server's own authorization checks.
fabric_role: Exposes capabilities through the narrowest Fabric MCP server.
foundry_role: Consumes tools with allow-lists and approval settings.
mcp_role: Standardizes capability access; it does not grant authority.
name: Governed MCP
offline_equivalent: Local FastMCP educational server with an allow-listed manifest.
summary: Typed MCP tools with owner, version, classification, limits, audit and revocation.
when_not_to_use: Exposing arbitrary shell, SQL, filesystem or URL access.
when_to_use: Sharing capabilities with many agents and developer tools.

authority: Layer-level permissions.
foundry_role: Consumes Gold through semantic models or data agents.
name: Medallion + AI
offline_equivalent: Local DuckDB medallion over synthetic data.
summary: Bronze preserves, Silver conforms, Gold serves semantic models and agents.
when_not_to_use: Never let agents read Bronze for business answers.
when_to_use: Every analytical foundation that agents will consume.

authority: Source credentials and Fabric permissions; RLS/OLS are not propagated.
name: Mirroring / Open Mirroring + AI
summary: Replicate operational data into OneLake and plan for recovery explicitly.
when_not_to_use: As a backup or disaster-recovery mechanism (not documented as one).
when_to_use: Near-real-time operational data for analytics and agents.

authority: Model permissions and RLS/OLS.
mcp_role: Fabric IQ MCP (query) and Power BI Authoring MCP (authoring).
name: Direct Lake + semantic model + AI
offline_equivalent: Local semantic model contract evaluated with DuckDB.
summary: Semantic models over OneLake tables give agents governed measures and relationships.
when_not_to_use: When tables are not yet modeled with clear grain and keys.
when_to_use: Governed measures for reports and agents.

authority: Domain owners.
name: Multi-domain is not multi-agent
summary: Add agents only where tools, context, policy, ownership or lifecycle truly differ.
when_not_to_use: Splitting agents only because there are several data domains.
when_to_use: Deciding agent boundaries.

authority: Entra, RBAC and network controls.
name: Secure enterprise Foundry + Fabric
summary: Private networking, managed identity, Key Vault, monitoring and policy around the solution.
when_not_to_use: Treating the demo topology as production.
when_to_use: Production deployments.

authority: Gateway policies plus backend authorization.
foundry_role: Model and agent endpoints behind the gateway.
mcp_role: REST APIs exposed as governed MCP tools.
name: APIM AI, MCP and tool governance
summary: A central gateway for authentication, quotas, routing, versioning and telemetry.
when_not_to_use: A single app and a single model, where the gateway adds only latency and cost.
when_to_use: Many consumers, shared quotas or a central tool registry.

authority: Release owners.
name: Evaluation + observability
offline_equivalent: Deterministic local evaluation against committed baselines.
summary: Traces and evaluations become quality gates for agents and data.
when_not_to_use: Never optional for production.
when_to_use: Always, before and after release.

authority: The environment's fallback policy.
mcp_role: Local server as the offline counterpart.
name: LIVE / HYBRID / OFFLINE resilience
summary: A provider router with breakers and approved fallback keeps the demo and the lesson alive.
when_not_to_use: Silently replacing live writes with simulation (never allowed).
when_to_use: Demos, workshops and degraded operations.

authority: Overlay owners; real identifiers stay in git-ignored files.
name: Customer overlay
summary: Configuration controls industry, domains, tools, policy, thresholds and learning modules.
when_not_to_use: Forking core code per customer.
when_to_use: Reusing the accelerator for another customer or industry.

authority: The developer's identity and workspace role.
mcp_role: Fabric MCP servers with hardened allow-lists.
name: Copilot CLI + Fabric Skills + MCP
offline_equivalent: Skills read locally plus the local MCP server.
summary: A terminal agent follows Microsoft-authored Fabric skills and calls Fabric MCP or REST.
when_not_to_use: Production changes without a reviewed pull request.
when_to_use: Fast exploration, triage and operator workflows.

authority: Pull-request review and branch protection.
name: Repo-first (Git as source of truth)
summary: Agents edit notebooks, TMDL and pipeline definitions in Git; CI validates; deployment applies.
when_not_to_use: One-off exploration.
when_to_use: Anything that must be reviewable, repeatable and auditable.

authority: Pull-request reviewers.
mcp_role: Read-only servers only (no per-call approval in the cloud agent).
name: Cloud agent issue to pull request
summary: A well-scoped issue becomes a pull request from the Copilot cloud agent with read-only tools.
when_not_to_use: Tasks that need live writes or tenant secrets.
when_to_use: A backlog of well-defined data-engineering tasks.

authority: Reviewers and CI gates.
name: Parallel agentic migration
summary: Many isolated agent sessions convert legacy notebooks or pipelines into reviewable pull requests.
when_not_to_use: Without automated validation of every change.
when_to_use: Bulk conversions with strong CI gates.

authority: Human reviewers keep approval authority.
name: Headless agent review in CI
summary: A non-interactive agent reviews notebooks and models in pull requests.
when_not_to_use: As the only reviewer for high-risk changes.
when_to_use: Consistent automated review alongside human review.

authority: On-behalf-of user identity plus approvals.
fabric_role: Governed context and approved write targets.
name: Embedded data-engineering assistant
summary: An internal app embeds an agent runtime that calls Fabric tools under app identity or on behalf of the user.
when_not_to_use: When an existing developer tool suffices.
when_to_use: A product experience for many users.

authority: Repository policy, human review and the existing governed change flow remain authoritative.
fabric_role: Supplies governed data contracts and explicit workspace acceptance criteria.
foundry_role: Supplies reasoning and evaluation requirements; it does not define deployment authority.
mcp_role: Tools may collect read-only facts and evidence; no specification grants tool authorization.
name: Spec-driven Fabric and Foundry delivery
offline_equivalent: Review a synthetic use-case specification, map requirements to tests and run existing offline gates.
summary: A reviewed specification connects business outcomes, architecture, implementation tasks and measurable verification before a PoC changes a workspace.
when_not_to_use: A typo, narrow repair with a clear reproduction, or an ordinary demo run with an existing approved plan.
when_to_use: New use cases or cross-layer changes with ambiguous requirements, contracts and governance decisions.
